newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH ELECTRICITY USE SEEN 102-118 TWH 2025 - KTM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH ELECTRICITY USE SEEN 102-118 TWH 2025 - KTM.

text.p: Finnish electricity consumption is projected to increase to between 102 terawatt hours (TWh) and 118 TWh by the year 2025 from almost 70 TWh now, the ministry of trade and industry (KTM) said in a report on Tuesday.

The report plotted five energy scenarios, all based on average annual economic growth of 2.5 percent, KTM said, noting that in 1965-95, Finnish annual economic growth had been on average about three percent.
In the high-consumption scenario, the assumption was that
the pace of growth would not be affected by regulations on the
supply or price of energy, KTM said.
It gave the following figures for that so called market
scenario: Change, pct/yr
Primary energy (Mtoe)* 31.7 39 44 1.4 0.9
Electricity use (TWh) 68.9 96 118 2.3 1.4
(*million tonnes oil equivalent)
The low-consumption scenario assumed that energy taxation
would tighten considerably and that the rise in consumption
would slow due to new more efficient technologies, KTM said.
It gave the following figures for that so called policy
scenario: Change, pct/yr
Primary energy (Mtoe)* 31.7 37 37 1.0 0.1
Electricity use (TWh) 68.9 92 102 2.0 0.7
In any scenario Finland would need to build new electricity
production capacity, KTM said.
In the high-consumption scenario, the need for new capacity would be "significant" -- 30 TWh or more than 5,000 megawatts -- in addition to extending current import agreements, KTM said.
In the low-consumption scenario, the need for additional production capacity would be slightly over 10 TWh, it said.

"All in all, the need to build (energy facilities) would be bigger in both scenarios because a majority of ageing heating plants should be replaced before the end of the period under review," the ministry added.
